newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Granite falls on negative rights reaction.
newsitem.headline: Granite falls on negative rights reaction.

text.p: Shares of Malaysian property developer and construction company Granite Industries Bhd fell sharply on Monday following a negative reaction to its proposed rights issue, analysts said.
Granite shares had fallen 26 cents to 3.44 ringgit at the midday break, reaching a new low for the year of 3.10 ringgit.

"The shares are falling because of its proposed rights issue. It will have an earnings dilution effect, but also it has prompted people to look at the fundamentals of the company," said an analyst at a foreign brokerage house.
Granite officials could not be immediately reached for comment.
The proceeds of the rights issue would be used to finance the subscription of shares in various leisure projects on the resort island of Langkawi in Kedah.

"Investors don't like the fact that the proceeds are being used to buy the exhibition hall and the Langkasuka Resort. they feel 176 million ringgit is too expensive a price," said another analyst who declined to be named.
The company announced on Friday it proposed to raise at least 300 million ringgit ($133.3 million) to finance its expansion plans in northern Kedah state.
The three-for-five rights issue would amount to 133.8 million shares of 50 cents each at an offer price of 2.30 ringgit each.
